objective: The Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Karnataka Act 27 of 2017) was enacted to make a provision for levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services or both by the Government of Karnataka. The new tax regime had faced certain difficulties. In order to overcome the difficulties, it is proposed to amend the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 Karnataka Act No. 27 of (2017). The proposed Karnataka Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2024, inter alia, provides for the following, namely:- (1) Clause (61) of section (2) and section 20 of the Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 is being amended so as to create a clear distinction between the input service distribution transactions requiring the transfer of input tax credit related to the invoices for receipt of services received on behalf of distinct persons and actual supply of services from one distinct person to another and make it compulsory to distribute the credit. (2) section 122A is being inserted to enable the levy of penalty for non- registration of machines used in the manufacture of tobacco products and pan masala. Hence, the Bill. 4
